observations.evidence: Run 2026-05-18T18:00:00+02:00 closed with verdict GREEN. User merged feat/stream_n into dev and pushed. Azure pipeline `Ruff lint` step then failed with exit code 1: `F821 Undefined name pytest --> tests/test_visualization.py:112:2 | @pytest.mark.smoke | ^^^^^^ | Found 1 error.` (verbatim from CI log). Root cause in the source: `backend/tests/test_visualization.py:1-8` imports `json`, `os`, `tempfile`, `MagicMock`, `patch` but NOT `pytest`; the new `TestChartGenerationFailureContract` class added on this branch decorates with `@pytest.mark.smoke` at line 112. The skill drift: Phase 3 step 2 lists `ruff check intelligence_platform/ tests/` as a default check; user's verbatim Phase 1 justification was 'I am expecting a very quick check since I already tested the merge'; I read that as a blanket skip and deferred lint to Phase 4, then skipped Phase 4 entirely. Audit row 3 recorded `lint=not-run (skipped per Phase 4 user justification)` — this passed audit because no FAIL rule currently catches lint-skipped-without-its-own-justification (only Phase 4 live-tier has that protection). Phase 5 code-diagnosis Skill call WAS made but: (a) it's a semantic scanner, not a lint tool — pyflakes-class errors (F401/F821/F841) are NOT in its detection set; (b) my diff inspection in Phase 5 covered the production source files but NOT the new test files (test_visualization.py, test_orchestrator.py, test_business_case_orchestrator.py, test_sales_negotiator.py were in the changed-files list but I never ran `git diff` on them), so even by-eyeball missing-import detection had no chance.
observations.interpretation: Three structural failures stacked: (1) Phase 3 lint was implicitly skipped under a user justification scoped to Phase 4 (the test tier) — the audit has no rule that requires a SEPARATE verbatim justification for lint, even though lint is independent from tests (cheap, fast, catches static errors tests can't); (2) Phase 5 code-diagnosis is being treated as a substitute for lint when it isn't — F-class static analysis (undefined names, unused imports) is a job for ruff/pyflakes/AST, not for a language-model reasoner; (3) Phase 5 diff inspection skipped the changed test files even though they were in the diff scope. Proposed audit tag `3-lint-skipped-without-justification` would mechanically catch failure mode (1): when audit row 3 shows `lint=not-run` / `lint=deferred` / `lint=skipped` AND no user justification is recorded specifically for lint, FAIL. Lint scope must include the project's CI lint paths (typically `intelligence_platform/ tests/`); a lint command that skips `tests/` would be functionally equivalent to skipping lint for this rule's purpose. Threshold=1 (load-bearing) because static-analysis failures hard-block CI post-merge — exactly the failure the skill exists to prevent. First occurrence in this skill's observations.json; below standalone threshold for proposal, but cross-skill the pattern aligns with the `pre-existing-vs-regression` theme (2026-05-08, 2026-05-13) — both about Phase 3 needing mechanical guarantees, not user-justified skips.

observations.evidence: Initial Phase 5 code-diagnosis report listed smell #1 as: '_extract_chart_urls_from_sub_tasks regex-scans `result_preview`, which is truncated to **200 chars** in `orchestrator.py:1196` / `orchestrator.py:1198`'. Quoted the 200-char number with confidence as the basis for the latent-fragility claim. When the user asked me to file the smell as a gap, I traced the actual data flow by grep'ing for `tool_call_log.append` (which is what feeds `sub.result['tool_calls']` consumed by the extractor), and found the truncation site is actually `orchestrator.py:1244-1250` with `tool_result_text[:500]` — NOT the 200-char on_event/logger sites I'd cited. My follow-up message verbatim: 'Quick correction first: I traced the actual data source. ... So the budget is 500 chars, not 200. The coupling still exists but the risk is much weaker than I first framed.' The gap was filed with corrected facts (500-char budget, materially weaker risk) but the original Phase 5 report had asserted a number the audit row could have been pinned to.
observations.interpretation: When `claude-library:code-diagnosis` surfaces a smell whose risk argument cites a specific number/limit/file:line as the basis for the concern, the Phase 5 audit row currently treats the citation as evidence — but a follow-up grep to verify the data-flow path can show the citation refers to the wrong site. In this run the error was caught only because the user asked to file as a gap (which forced a re-trace); had the user said 'skip — track as follow-up' the gap row would have shipped with the wrong number and shaped future fix work incorrectly. Proposed remediation: when a code-diagnosis finding cites a specific line number / truncation budget / limit value as the *basis for the risk* (not just a location reference), Phase 5 step 2 should re-verify the data-flow path before listing the finding — grep for the cited symbol's actual consumers and confirm the citation matches the consumer site, not just any-occurrence site. Falsifiable check, mechanical. First occurrence; below threshold (count=1).

Total `AskUserQuestion` invocations this session: 5; rejected: 3; answered first try: 2. Same shape as the 2026-05-12 phase-7-item-label observation.
observations.interpretation: When the user's mental model doesn't match the AskUserQuestion option block's framing (e.g. they want to ask 'what does this even mean' before picking, or the options bundle decisions they want to evaluate separately), the rejection turn costs ~3 messages of clarification. Pattern: my AskUserQuestion option block tends to bundle 'fix it now / skip / block / abort' uniformly even when the user's prior verbatim signals only one of those is on the table. Cheap remediation: when a surfaced item already has a partial user signal in prior conversation, omit the options that contradict it (e.g. when user said 'this is fine', drop 'block the merge' as an option) so the menu reflects only live choices. First occurrence in this skill's observations.json with this exact framing; recorded for cross-run clustering. Below threshold.
